content: 1. Strong CYP3A inducers significantly reduce the systemic exposure of eliglustat. Co-administration of these drugs is not recommended. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Elranatamab increases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Elranatamab can cause cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which may suppress CYP enzyme activity, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. This effect is most likely to occur during the initiation of elranatamab step-up dosing, up to 14 days after the first treatment dose, and during or after CRS. Close monitoring is required. 4. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Co-administration of CYP3A inducers with elvitegravir may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Phenobarbital decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in loss of virologic response and resistance. 8. Enasidenib decreases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Enasidenib, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the systemic exposure of CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor and adjust the dose of the substrate as clinically indicated. 10. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of encorafenib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of enfortumab vedotin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of enoxaparin by increasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of entrectinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of enzalutamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Epcoritamab increases the release of cytokines, which may suppress CYP enzyme activity, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. For certain CYP substrates, even minimal changes in their concentrations can result in serious adverse reactions. Modify therapy as recommended in the substrate's prescribing information and monitor closely. 16. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while ephedrine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 17. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while epinephrine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 18. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while racemic epinephrine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 19. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of eplerenone by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by altering metabolism. Avoid co-administration of strong CYP2C9 or CYP3A4 inducers with erdafitinib. 21. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ergotamine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erlotinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin base by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of escitalopram by affecting hepatic CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of eslicarbazepine acetate by increasing its metabolism. Higher dosages of eslicarbazepine may be necessary. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of esmolol by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration of phenobarbital. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. 30. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Phenobarbital and estazolam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of estropipate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Phenobarbital and eszopiclone both increase sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Phenobarbital and ethanol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive use is recommended. 40. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ethosuximide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Ethosuximide decreases the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethotoin by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Phenobarbital may occasionally not change or even increase phenytoin levels via competitive inhibition. Monitor closely. 43. Etomidate and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of etoposide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Phenobarbital decreases the levels of etravirine by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Phenobarbital and eucalyptus both increase sedation. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of everolimus by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of exemestane by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. For patients receiving exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose of exemestane is 50 mg daily after a meal. 50. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of fedratinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of felbamate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Felbamate increases phenobarbital levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of fenfluramine by an unspecified mechanism. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while fenfluramine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 55. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to reduced fentanyl plasma concentrations, lack of efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in physically dependent patients. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 56. Phenobarbital and fentanyl both increase sedation. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatment options are inadequate.
